title: PROBATIONERS OF INDIAN POLICE SERVICE CALL ON THE PRESIDENT
subtitle: POLICE OFFICERS SHOULD RE-ORIENT THEIR APPROACH TOWARDS CYBER CRIMES: PRESIDENT DROUPADI MURMU TO IPS Probationers
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                10 NOV 2026 3:21PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Probationers of the Indian Police Service 78 RR (2025 batch) called on the President of India, Smt Droupadi Murmu at Rashtrapati Bhavan today (November 10, 2026).
Addressing the probationers, the President said that for the citizens, police officers and constables are symbols of governance. People perceive the governance to be good when the police system functions well.  People feel immensely supported when a police officer listens to their grievances with sensitivity and attentiveness. She urged the IPS officers to prioritise alleviating the fears of socially or economically weaker individuals who generally lack access to senior officials, and addressing their grievances.
The President stated that some of the employees in the system may be more proficient in the use of technology than the senior officers. She advised the officer trainees to not hesitate to learn even from the most junior members of their team. She urged them to encourage public participation and teamwork in their working style. She said that by prioritising the welfare of their team members, they will enhance their capabilities and enthusiasm.
The President stated that the police officers would derive a high level of authority from the laws and rules related to policing. However, they will earn real respect from the people, based on their performance and value system. She said that they should have a sense of commitment to serving citizens rather than a sense of superiority over them.
The President said that spreading misinformation to trigger fear among the people is emerging as a serious issue. Impressionable minds, especially the youth, can be swayed by orchestrated disinformation. This kind of orchestrated mischief can happen at local, regional, or even national levels. Smart policing can prevent such situations from getting too challenging and big.
The President said that cyber-crimes are getting widespread and more serious. The police have to sensitise society more extensively about the gravity of cybercrimes. She emphasised that the police officers should reorient their own approach towards such crimes. Deep-fake content poses new threats to people. She highlighted the need for police officers to always stay ahead of the criminals who use state-of-the-art technologies.

content:
The Ministry of Ayush has made significant progress under Special Campaign 6.0, with a strong focus on timely grievance redressal, efficient record management and cleanliness across its offices.
During the campaign, the Ministry disposed of 368 public grievances and 64 public grievance appeals, reaffirming its commitment to responsive, transparent and citizen-centric governance. Additionally, 7 references from Members of Parliament and 4 references from the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) were addressed, reflecting the Ministry’s emphasis on timely and effective grievance redressal.
As part of the campaign, the Ministry conducted 285 cleanliness campaigns, aimed at improving workplace cleanliness, promoting a hygienic working environment and making better use of office space.
In the area of record management, 1,610 files were reviewed, weeded out and closed. Through the disposal of scrap and obsolete records, a total of 8,741 square feet of space was freed, making it available for more productive use. The Ministry also earned ₹1,94,161 in revenue through scrap disposal, reflecting its efforts towards better resource management and improved administrative efficiency.
The Ministry of Ayush continues to implement Special Campaign 6.0 with an emphasis on the timely disposal of pending grievances and appeals, systematic record management, cleanliness and effective use of government resources. Through these initiatives, the Ministry aims to build a cleaner, more organised and citizen-centric working environment.

title: Odisha charts a National Roadmap for Millet led Agricultural Transformation
subtitle:
Dr. M.L. Jat Emphasises Expansion of Millet Cultivation Area to 5 Lakh Hectares with Production Target of 8 Lakh Metric Tonnes by 2047

Two days National Event on Agro-Biodiversity Conservation, Climate-Resilient Agriculture and Sustainable Food Systems Begins in Bhubaneswar
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                10 NOV 2026 6:18PM by PIB Delhi
content:
A two day national event on agro-biodiversity conservation, climate-resilient agriculture and sustainable food systems was commenced on 10th November 2026 at Bhubaneswar, Odisha, in the presence of
Shri Braj Mohan Ram, Governor of Odisha, Shri Kanak Vardhan Singh Deo, Minister for Agriculture and Farmer Welfare, Government of Odisha, Dr. Mangi Lal Jat, Secretary DARE and Director General, ICAR, Dr. Soumya Swaminathan, Chairperson, M.S. Swaminathan Research Foundation; and Shri Sachin Ramachandra Jadhav, IAS, Commissioner-cum-Secretary, Department of Agriculture and Farmers' Empowerment, Government of Odisha
, along with eminent agricultural scientists, policymakers and other stakeholders.
The inaugural session marked the formal commencement of event, followed by visit to exhibition stalls and display of agricultural innovations, indigenous crop diversity, millet-based products and interaction with farmers.
Addressing the gathering, Dr Jat emphasised on use of rich agrobiodiversity of Odisha through a greater focus on opportunity crops including millets to address the grand challenges of climate change, soil health, nutrition etc while promoting local food system for one health.
Dr. Jat, also highlighted the success of Odisha Shree Anna Abhiyan and its potential to emerge as a national model for millet-based agricultural transformation. He stressed on the area expansion of millet cultivation from 1.79 lakh ha to 5 lakh ha by 2047 with a production target of 8 lakh metric tonnes. The state achievement in ragi procurement, with 7.5 lakh quintals during KMS 2024-25 and a target of 8 lakh quintals for 2025-26 and importance of conserving indigenous millet diversity, particularly the 163 documented finger millet landraces, and promoting traditional varieties such as Kalia, Bati, Mami and Bharathi were appreciated.
Further, Dr. Jat discussed on scaling up scientific cultivation practices, promoting minor millets such as suan and kangu, developing affordable processing machinery, strengthening FPOs and women's SHGs, and expanding millet-based enterprises and market linkages through ICAR-IIMR, Hyderabad. He also proposed about the strengthening research collaboration between ICAR-IIMR, Hyderabad and for establishment of Centre of Excellence on Millets at Odisha University of Agriculture and Technology.
The event aimed to strengthen institutional partnerships, promote knowledge exchange and accelerate Odisha's journey towards sustainable, climate-resilient and economically viable millet-based agricultural development.

title: Union Minister of State For Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare Shri Ram Nath Thakur participates in Khet Bachao Abhiyan in North 24 Parganas
subtitle: The Minister emphasises on Natural Farming for Soil Protection and Sustainable Agriculture
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                10 NOV 2026 5:27PM by PIB Kolkata
content:
Kolkata; November 10, 2026
As part of the nationwide Khet Bachao Abhiyan, the Union Minister of State for Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare, Shri Ram Nath Thakur participated in a programme organised by the ICAR-National Institute of Natural Fibre Engineering and Technology (ICAR-NINFET) at Subhasnagar, in Swarupnagar Block of North 24 Parganas district, West Bengal.
The programme underscored the Government of India's commitment to protecting agricultural land, restoring soil health and promoting natural farming as a sustainable approach to agriculture. It highlighted the importance of conserving soil resources, reducing excessive dependence on chemical inputs and encouraging environmenta-friendly farming practices for the benefit of the present and future generations.
While addressing the gathering, the Union Minister harped on returning to natural farming and least utilisation of chemical fertiliser, so as to keep the soil health intact. He highlighted natural farming as an important approach to maintaining soil fertility, improving soil health and promoting ecological balance. He also encouraged farmers to adopt climate-resilient agricultural methods, scientific innovations and modern technologies to ensure long-term agricultural productivity and sustainability.
The Minister also stressed on the importance of conserving soil as a living resource and adopting balanced, need-based agricultural input management. He urged farmers to make effective utilisation of Soil Health Cards for informed fertiliser application, improved nutrient-use efficiency and the maintenance of soil fertility. In this regard, he highlighted the role of Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs) in providing technical guidance, practical demonstrations and extension services to facilitate the adoption of sustainable and natural farming practices.
The Union Minister urged the farmers to return to extend processes of farming, including utilisation of organic fertilisers an organic pesticides, to boost natural farming as well as aiding in reaps which are healthy for living.
The event was organised by ICAR-NINFET.
The programme reinforced the central message of Khet Bachao Abhiyan for Ravi crops, going on from October 22, to November 30, 2026 in the entire country- healthy soil is the foundation of healthy crops, sustainable agriculture and farmers' prosperity. Promoting natural farming, conserving soil fertility and adopting environmentally sustainable agricultural practices are essential to safeguarding agricultural resources and ensuring long-term food and livelihood security.

title: Bharat Mobility Expo gaining global recognition, third edition to be the second largest such expo in the world: Commerce and Industry Minister Shri Piyush Goyal
subtitle:
Shri Piyush Goyal urges mobility industry to tap global markets and expand India's manufacturing footprint

Shri Goyal calls for positioning India as the world's manufacturing hub through global partnerships and export-led growth

India well on track to achieve $1 trillion export target this year; engineering sector records 22 per cent growth: Shri Goyal
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                10 NOV 2026 9:48PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister of Commerce & Industry Shri Piyush Goyal today, speaking at the Curtain Raiser of the third edition of Bharat Mobility Global Expo in New Delhi, highlighted the growing stature of the event and the importance of the mobility sector to India's manufacturing and global economic ambitions.
He urged industry stakeholders across the mobility value chain to look beyond the domestic market and tap global markets and export opportunities. He said that complementing India's large domestic market with international markets would enable businesses to achieve economies of scale and become globally competitive in pricing. Expressing confidence in the capabilities of Indian manufacturers, he said that those supplying to Japanese and European automobile manufacturers, as well as the aerospace and defence sectors, had the potential to meet world-class quality standards.
Recalling the initial discussions on the concept of Bharat Mobility, Shri Goyal said that the initiative had brought together different segments of the mobility ecosystem, which had traditionally organised separate exhibitions at different times and locations, often attracting the same set of visitors. He said that bringing the entire ecosystem under one roof had been made possible by the availability of Bharat Mandapam and Yashobhoomi, developed with the vision of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi to make India an international exhibition destination.
The Minister said that Bharat Mobility had demonstrated the strength of a whole-of-Government approach by breaking silos between departments, ministries and States, while also bringing together different industries associated with the mobility sector. These include steel, chemicals, electronics, two-wheelers, three-wheelers, four-wheelers, commercial and passenger vehicles, construction equipment and tyres.
Congratulating industry stakeholders on the success of the second edition, Shri Goyal expressed confidence that the third edition would be even bigger and better, potentially emerging as the world's largest mobility exhibition in terms of both size and visitors, including domestic and international visitors. He said that, depending on the demand for exhibition space and the expansion of facilities, Bharat Mobility could potentially become the largest event of its kind globally.
The Minister urged the organisers and industry to market the event extensively across the world and aim to attract at least 25,000 international visitors out of the expected 10 lakh visitors. He emphasised that the event should go beyond original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) and reach the wider global ecosystem, including tyre dealers, suppliers, auto component manufacturers and the substantial after-sales market.
Shri Goyal said that every segment represented at Bharat Mobility offered significant opportunities for international engagement and sourcing from India. He urged industry stakeholders to identify opportunities across individual sectors and countries, and to look at the entire global value chain. He said that failing to think on a global scale would undermine the considerable effort invested in organising Bharat Mobility.
Shri Goyal said that the only possible bottleneck to India's progress was the mindset and not the country's capabilities. He emphasised the need for industry to recognise and realise India's potential.
Sharing his experience of interactions with international industry leaders during overseas delegations, the Minister said that the interest and enthusiasm for India had been extraordinary. Referring to his recent visit to Japan, he said that the response from Japanese industry had been particularly encouraging, with several companies expressing interest in partnering with Indian manufacturers to serve global markets. He noted that the interest extended beyond small investments, with companies considering billion-dollar investments in India to manufacture products for the world.
He said that European manufacturers, which had traditionally focused on international markets, were increasingly recognising the challenges of competing globally given Europe's manufacturing costs and regulatory burden. Referring to the Free Trade Agreement (FTA) negotiations, the Minister said that market access in India would initially allow European automobile manufacturers to test demand by introducing a limited number of models in the Indian market. Once they identify models with adequate demand, manufacturers could establish production in India, not only to serve the domestic market but also to export to the rest of the world.
Shri Goyal said that manufacturing in India would enable companies to benefit from economies of scale, access the large domestic market and produce vehicles at competitive prices for global markets. This would create significant opportunities for Indian component manufacturers, startups, steel and rubber industries, and other participants across the mobility ecosystem. He urged industry stakeholders to capture these opportunities before other countries did.
The Minister underlined that India's large domestic market was a major advantage in attracting global manufacturing investments. Referring to automobile sales during the festive season, he said that one million cars had been sold during Navratri alone, while around 70,000 cars were sold over the two days of Dhanteras. He said that the scale of the Indian market offered an ideal opportunity for global manufacturers to establish production facilities in India and use the country as a base for serving international markets.
Urging the industry to build on the success of the first two editions, Shri Goyal called for the third edition to be larger in scale, more efficient and more technologically advanced. He said that the first two days of the exhibition had been reserved for businesses, business launches and new product launches, providing an opportunity for companies to showcase their quality and capabilities to the world.
He highlighted that bringing the entire mobility value chain together at one location made the event particularly attractive to international visitors, who could engage with different segments of the industry in a single visit. Recalling his experience as an entrepreneur around 40 years ago, when he visited Hanover to engage with the entire engineering ecosystem, the Minister said that India was now creating similar large-format platforms through Bharat Mobility, Bharat Tex, Startup Mahakumbh and Bharat BuildCon.
He said that these platforms, which bring together entire value chains, enabled India to showcase its capabilities to the world. Referring also to the convergence of India's telecom and electronics industries towards large exhibitions, Shri Goyal said that India was offering the world a scale that it had not witnessed before. He said that the theme "Beyond Boundaries" reflected the spirit of Bharat and the future envisaged for Indian industry.
Shri Goyal reiterated that India's target of achieving $1 trillion in exports this year was sacrosanct and said that the country was well on track to achieve it. Referring to the September export figures, he said that India had already achieved approximately $480 billion, accounting for 48 per cent of the annual target in the first six months. He noted that exports generally picked up in the second half of the year and expressed confidence in the country's export performance.
The Minister said that the October export figures would be shared by the Commerce Secretary on the 15th and indicated that the numbers would be encouraging. He expressed confidence that there would be no looking back thereafter and called upon industry to move beyond incremental growth and aim for greater expansion.
Highlighting the contribution of the engineering sector to export growth, Shri Goyal said that the sector had recorded growth of around 22 per cent. He urged industry to sustain this growth and make it a benchmark for the future rather than treating it as a one-time achievement.
The Minister said that the European Union's 27-nation bloc was expected to open up for Indian businesses at zero duty by March or April, providing further opportunities for Indian exporters in the coming year. He added that India was also negotiating with another seven to eight countries, which would further expand market access. Once these opportunities materialise, India would have preferential access to markets accounting for nearly 75 per cent of global GDP.
Shri Goyal urged industry to act early to capture emerging international opportunities, noting that countries across the world were competing for global markets and investments. He said that the Government had endeavoured to address the aspirations of industry by expanding market access and extending support through various initiatives.
He highlighted the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for the auto component industry and the PLI Scheme for specialty steel. He also referred to the Export Promotion Mission and urged industry stakeholders to make full use of the initiative to strengthen exports, market their products and build their industry brands.
Emphasising the wider significance of the mobility sector, Shri Goyal said that mobility was not merely about economic figures, production numbers or the sector's contribution to the economy, but also about transforming lives and fulfilling aspirations. Referring to World Bank data indicating that 50 crore people had moved out of extreme poverty in India over a period of 12 years, he said that one of the first aspirations of people moving up the economic ladder was to upgrade their mobility and transport.
He said that this transformation was visible in the shift from bicycles to two-wheelers and from two-wheelers to entry-level four-wheelers. As families and individuals moved up the economic ladder, their self-respect, self-esteem and desire to contribute to nation-building also increased. He noted the growth of the new middle class, the rising number of first-time passenger vehicle buyers and the expansion of highways and roads across the country.
The Minister also highlighted the growing attractiveness and affordability of electric mobility and said that the mobility sector would be among the biggest beneficiaries of India's position as the fastest-growing large economy. He called upon the industry to build the entire mobility ecosystem in India and make the country the manufacturing hub of the world, covering vehicles, components and mobility technologies.
Shri Goyal said that India should also emerge as a centre for developing technologies and creating designs, with all talent-driven solutions being centred around the country. He expressed confidence that the potential for growth across the mobility sector was immense and said that India should soon aspire to sell 10 million passenger vehicles domestically, with exports being additional to domestic sales.
Referring to the two-wheeler sector, the Minister noted that annual sales were already around 25 million units, excluding exports. He said that the potential across all segments of the mobility ecosystem was substantial and invited industry stakeholders to be part of India's growth journey by thinking big, planning ambitiously, pursuing collaborations, bringing in new technologies and supporting startups to introduce newer elements into their businesses.
The Minister also indicated that the growing demand for Bharat Mobility could require further expansion of exhibition infrastructure at Bharat Mandapam and Yashobhoomi. He said that exhibition space was likely to be fully booked and that the possibility of returning to temporary hangar facilities could not be ruled out.
He said that the demand witnessed during the third edition would be assessed to plan the next phase of expansion at both venues. The objective would be to provide at least one-and-a-half times, if not twice, the existing exhibition space by the time the fourth edition of Bharat Mobility was organised. He expressed confidence that by then the mobility industry would also be significantly more integrated with the global economy, enabling businesses to expand their international presence and market penetration.

title: Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh Chairs ESSC General Body Meeting, Emphasises Citizen-Centric Science Communication to Showcase India's Scientific Achievements
subtitle:

India’s Deep-Sea Exploration Is Advancing with MATSYA-6000 and Indo-French Collaboration, says Dr. Jitendra Singh

Ocean information services, polar expeditions and glacier research expand India's scientific capabilities and public utility: Dr. Jitendra Singh

date:

                10 NOV 2026 5:27PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology and Earth Sciences, and MoS PMO, Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh today chaired the Second General Body Meeting of the Earth System Sciences Council (ESSC), where he emphasised citizen-centric science communication and the need to transform India's scientific achievements into accessible, compelling narratives for the general public.
Calling for greater citizen-centric science communication, the Minister stressed that scientific breakthroughs, technological innovations and research outcomes must be conveyed in simple language that enables ordinary citizens to appreciate their relevance and national significance.
The meeting reviewed the annual reports and audited accounts for FY 2025-26 of the five constituent institutions of ESSC; National Institute of Ocean Technology (NIOT), Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services (INCOIS), National Centre for Earth Science Studies (NCESS), Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology (IITM) and National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR). Secretary, Ministry of Earth Sciences, Dr. T. Srinivasa Kumar; Director General, CSIR, Dr. N. Kalaiselvi; Joint Secretary, MoES, Dr. G.R.S. Rao; Additional Secretary & Financial Adviser, MoES, Chetan Prakash Jain; and senior scientists and officials of the Ministry and its institutions attended the meeting.
Dr. Jitendra Singh emphasised that professional communication expertise must complement scientific knowledge to make research and technological achievements more accessible to society. He encouraged greater coordination among institutional communication teams, regular interaction with media professionals and the use of creative formats to communicate scientific achievements, technological applications and public services more effectively.
Reviewing the progress of the Deep Ocean Mission, Dr. Jitendra Singh was apprised of major advances in India's human deep-sea exploration programme, including the development of MATSYA-6000, the country's 6,000-metre depth-rated human submersible. Indian aquanauts successfully completed dives to 4,025 metres and 5,002 metres during the Indo-French expedition aboard the submersible Nautile, marking a significant advancement in India's deep-sea exploration capabilities.
NIOT also reported progress in indigenous ocean technologies, including desalination solutions for Lakshadweep, offshore fish cage technologies, oceanographic instrumentation, deep-sea mineral exploration and ocean thermal energy conversion. These initiatives strengthen India's capabilities in ocean exploration, marine research and sustainable utilisation of ocean resources.
Dr. Jitendra Singh reviewed scientific advances under Mission Mausam and the PRITHVI programme, including developments in the Bharat Forecasting System, advanced numerical weather prediction and atmospheric observation networks.
IITM's research is strengthening weather and climate forecasting through improved modelling systems, expanded observation infrastructure and emerging Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning applications. These efforts are aimed at improving forecasting capabilities and strengthening India's scientific preparedness for weather and climate-related challenges.
The Minister reviewed INCOIS's expanding ocean information and advisory services for fishing communities, coastal populations and maritime stakeholders. Its services include multilingual marine advisories, fishing-related information, swell-surge inundation forecasts and ocean observation products, strengthening the application of ocean science in public service delivery and coastal preparedness.
NCESS presented its scientific contributions in earth sciences, including research on landslides, tectonic processes, ocean structures, atmospheric aerosols and rainfall over the Western Ghats, alongside the development of scientific laboratories and research facilities.
Dr. Jitendra Singh reviewed NCPOR's achievements in polar and ocean research, including the 45th Indian Antarctic Expedition involving 95 members, the 16th Indian Arctic Expedition, glacier monitoring in the Himalayas and scientific investigations in the Southern Ocean.
Research on polar environments, glacier dynamics, ocean-atmosphere interactions and carbon cycling continue to contribute to a deeper understanding of climate change and global environmental processes, strengthening India's contribution to international polar research.
In his concluding remarks, Dr. Jitendra Singh welcomed the suggestions and contributions of members and assured follow-up by the Ministry. He encouraged members to continue sharing ideas and suggestions with him, the Secretary and concerned officials beyond formal meetings, describing the institutions as an extended scientific family working collectively towards advancing India's Earth Sciences capabilities.

title: India reaffirms Commitment to Climate Multilateralism and a Fair, Ambitious Outcome at UNFCCC COP31, in Antalya (Türkiye)
subtitle:
Developed Countries need to fulfil Climate Finance Obligations under Article 9.1 of Paris Agreement, highlights India

Emphasis laid on Equity, Just Transition and Adaptation as central to addressing Climate Change, particularly for the Global South
ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                10 NOV 2026 1:11PM by PIB Delhi
content:
India has reaffirmed its commitment to climate multilateralism and the principles of Equity and Common But Differentiated Responsibilities and Respective Capabilities (CBDR-RC), calling for a fair, equitable and ambitious outcome at the 31st Conference of the Parties (COP31) to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC), being held in Antalya, Türkiye.
Delivering India's Opening Statement at the COP31, Secretary, Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Government of India, Shri Narendra Bhooshan expressed gratitude to Türkiye and Australia for their leadership of COP31. He commended all Parties and negotiating groups for their efforts towards strengthening climate multilateralism and stated that India aligns itself with the statements made by G77 and China, LMDC, and BASIC.
Emphasising the importance of multilateralism, India underlined that the UNFCCC and its Paris Agreement remain the most inclusive platforms where every country has a voice. India reaffirmed its faith in this process, rooted in equity and the principle of CBDR-RC. Welcoming the Presidency's vision of a ‘COP of Implementation’, guided by Dialogue, Consensus and Action, India noted that dialogue builds trust, consensus ensures collective ownership of outcomes, and action translates commitments into progress on the ground.
Highlighting the growing challenges posed by the prospect of crossing 1.5°C warming, India stressed that equity has become particularly urgent to ensure that no one is left behind in the collective effort to address climate change. India reiterated its commitment to contributing its fair share to global climate action while pursuing the development and well-being of its people. It also underscored that just transition and meeting adaptation needs remain significant challenges, particularly for the Global South, where these are closely intertwined with the challenge of development itself.
On climate finance, India emphasised that public finance from developed countries remains central to catalysing climate action in developing countries and strengthening adaptation finance flows to address their vulnerabilities. It underscored the fundamental importance of Article 9.1 of the Paris Agreement, which establishes the obligation of developed countries to provide financial resources to developing countries. Reaffirming its constructive engagement at COP31, India stated that it would work with all Parties towards achieving a fair, equitable and ambitious outcome.

title: Island fisheries at the centre of India’s Blue Economy push
subtitle: Lakshadweep and Andaman & Nicobar Islands to anchor growth in tuna, seaweed and ornamental fisheries
ministry: Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                10 NOV 2026 10:06AM by PIB Delhi
content:
India is endowed with a vast and diverse marine resource base, supported by a coastline of approximately 11,099 km and an Exclusive Economic Zone of nearly 24 lakh sq. km. With an estimated marine fisheries potential of 58.6 lakh MT within its EEZ, the sector plays a vital role in sustaining the livelihoods of nearly 50 lakh fishers, while contributing significantly to food security, nutrition, employment, income generation and export earnings. India today ranks among the leading fisheries and aquaculture producing nations globally, with seafood exports valued at around ₹73,890 crore during FY 2025-26, underscoring the sector’s growing importance in the national economy and global seafood trade. India’s fisheries sector is evolving from a production-focused activity into a dynamic, technology-driven and value-oriented pillar of the national economy. Since 2015, the Government of India has significantly stepped-up public investment in the fisheries sector, committing Rs. 39,272 crore through key schemes and programmes.
Under PMMSY, substantial investments have been envisaged for the island territories to strengthen fisheries development. Andaman & Nicobar Islands have been allocated an investment of
₹218 crore
, while
Lakshadweep
has been earmarked
₹175 crore
, reflecting the Government’s commitment to unlocking the fisheries potential of these strategically important maritime regions.
This focus on island-led fisheries development was also reflected in the Union Budget 2025-26, which outlined an enabling framework for the sustainable harnessing of fisheries resources from the Exclusive Economic Zone and the High Seas, with special emphasis on Lakshadweep and the Andaman & Nicobar Islands. The emphasis marks a clear recognition of the strategic importance of these island territories in accessing underutilised marine fish resources within the Indian EEZ and adjacent High Seas, while placing sustainability and scientific management at the centre of future expansion.
Lakshadweep and the Andaman & Nicobar Islands occupy a distinctive position in India’s marine geography. Together accounting for nearly 40% of the country’s Exclusive Economic Zone, the two island groups extend India’s presence across the Arabian Sea and the Bay of Bengal, with access to rich oceanic fishing grounds and major tuna migration routes. Lakshadweep’s lagoon systems, coral reefs and surrounding deep-sea waters offer favourable conditions for tuna fisheries, seaweed cultivation and reef-based livelihoods. The Andaman & Nicobar Islands, with their extensive coastline, diverse marine habitats and proximity to Southeast Asian maritime routes, provide similar opportunities for expanding sustainable fisheries, mariculture and value-added seafood production. Their ecological richness and strategic location make these islands central to India’s efforts to build a more diversified and ocean-based fisheries economy.
Tuna the development has emerged as the centrepiece of the Government’s strategic roadmap for high-value marine fisheries. The waters surrounding Lakshadweep and the Andaman & Nicobar Islands harbour substantial underutilised stocks of Yellowfin, Skipjack and Bigeye tuna, offering strong potential for sustainable, export-oriented fisheries. The Government is advancing a science-based and value-chain driven approach that integrates modern deep-sea vessels, selective fishing methods such as hook and line and pole and line, improved onboard handling, cold-chain expansion, processing and canning facilities, and efficient export linkages. In Lakshadweep, a five-year plan seeks to double tuna production to 50,000 tonnes, supported by the induction of deep-sea vessels, mother vessels and the islands’ traditional, ecologically sound pole and line fishery. In the Andaman & Nicobar Islands, a dedicated Tuna Cluster under PMMSY is accelerating fleet modernisation and infrastructure development, including new vessels, upgraded fishing fleets and expanded cold storage capacity, while MPEDA’s strengthened presence is expected to improve market access and facilitate direct exports from the islands.
Beyond Tuna value chain development, the Government is also advancing seaweed and ornamental fisheries as complementary pillars of the island economy, broadening the fisheries growth model beyond capture fisheries alone. Lakshadweep’s clean lagoon systems and the coral-rich ecosystems of the Andaman & Nicobar Islands offer favourable conditions for sustainable seaweed cultivation, with potential applications across food, nutraceuticals, cosmetics, pharmaceuticals and bio-industrial products. With Lakshadweep notified as a dedicated Seaweed Cluster, the roadmap envisages large-scale cultivation, seed banks, hatcheries and capacity building to develop a reliable seaweed value chain. Ornamental fisheries add another high-value opportunity, particularly in Lakshadweep, which hosts over 300 reef-associated ornamental species. The strategic plan focuses on establishing medium-scale rearing units, promoting conservation-based and regulated collection practices, and improving market access for sustainably sourced aquarium species, thereby creating diversified livelihood opportunities for island communities while safeguarding fragile marine ecosystems.
To enable these emerging areas of growth, modernising fisheries infrastructure has become a key element of the Government’s approach in the island territories. Investments are being channelled into facilities across the value chain, including fish landing centres, ice plants, cold-chain networks, onboard preservation systems, fish aggregating devices, boat-building yards, value-addition units and systems to support export facilitation. These measures are intended to build local capacity, reduce post-harvest losses and improve the readiness of island-based fisheries to access domestic and export markets.
Taken together, these interventions indicate a long-term effort to place India’s island territories at the centre of a more diversified and sustainable marine economy. By linking tuna fisheries, seaweed cultivation, ornamental fisheries, infrastructure development, research support and market access, the strategy seeks to move beyond resource extraction towards value creation within the islands. Its success will depend on balancing production growth with ecological safeguards, while ensuring that fishers, local enterprises and island communities are able to participate meaningfully in emerging domestic and export value chains.

title: New AIIMS cross 6 crore OPD consultations since 2021-22, expanding access to specialised tertiary healthcare across India
subtitle:
22 new AIIMS approved under Pradhan Mantri Swasthya Suraksha Yojana (PMSSY), 18 fully functional institutions providing comprehensive healthcare, medical education and research services

Expansion of AIIMS under PMSSY addresses regional imbalances in affordable and reliable tertiary healthcare, and strengthens medical education and research

OPD consultations at new AIIMS rise from 50.03 lakh in 2021-22 to 144.96 lakh in 2025-26, reflecting increased utilisation of specialised healthcare services
ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                10 NOV 2026 6:05PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The new All India Institutes of Medical Sciences (AIIMS) established under the Pradhan Mantri Swasthya Suraksha Yojana (PMSSY) have collectively recorded over 6 crore Outpatient Department (OPD) consultations in the five-year period since 2021-22, as on 31st October 2026. The achievement reflects the growing reach of these institutions and their contribution to bringing specialised tertiary healthcare services closer to people across the country.
The Government of India has been expanding the AIIMS network under PMSSY to address regional disparities in the availability of affordable and reliable tertiary healthcare. The initiative has also sought to strengthen the country's medical education and research ecosystem alongside the expansion of specialised healthcare services.
Of the 22 new AIIMS approved under PMSSY in various phases, 18 are fully functional. These institutions provide a range of services spanning OPD and Inpatient Department (IPD) care, emergency and trauma services, diagnostics, medical education and research.
The growing utilisation of these institutions is reflected in the year-wise OPD figures. Consultations increased from 50.03 lakh in 2021-22 to 77.95 lakh in 2022-23 and 100.52 lakh in 2023-24, reaching 129.98 lakh in 2024-25 and 144.96 lakh in 2025-26. During 2026-27, the new AIIMS recorded 97.41 lakh OPD patients till October 2026. The cumulative figures across these years amount to approximately 6.01 crore.
The new AIIMS have also expanded opportunities for undergraduate, postgraduate and nursing education, while developing specialised clinical facilities and advanced medical services. Together, these institutions are contributing to the expansion of India's medical education and research infrastructure.

The Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) has successfully concluded

,
conducted from
2nd to 31st October, 2026
.
Under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi and guidance of Home Minister Shri Amit Shah, the month-long campaign focused on promoting cleanliness and efficient office management, expediting the disposal of pending matters, addressing public grievances and improving the overall functioning of the Ministry and its organisations. Special emphasis was laid on field and outstation offices having direct public interface.
Under Special Campaign 6, Ministry of Home Affairs achieved significant progress in disposal of pending matters, cleanliness and efficient office management. The campaign commenced with a preparatory phase on 15th September 2026, followed by its implementation from 2nd to 31st October 2026, across the Ministry of Home Affairs and its Attached and Subordinate Offices throughout the country.
The campaign was closely monitored at the highest level, with active participation from all Divisions of the Ministry, Central Armed Police Forces (CAPFs) and affiliated organisations. Regular progress reports were uploaded on the Special Campaign Portal, hosted by the Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG).
A total of 6757 sites were initially identified for the Swachhata campaign, which was subsequently expanded to cover 7,963 sites. The major achievements of the campaign are as follows:
Disposal of references and grievances:
147 references from Members of Parliament, 141 references from State Governments, 11,902 public grievances and 1,666 appeals were disposed of.
Review of records:
2,19,644 physical files and 30,385 electronic files were reviewed.
Space management:
78,125 square feet of office space was freed through effective record management and disposal of redundant material.
Revenue generation:
Over ₹10.17 crore was generated through the disposal of scrap, out of which ₹2.63 crore through e-waste disposal.
Social media outreach:
Around 1,200 posts carrying the hashtag
#SpecialCampaign6
were shared across various social media platforms, including X, Instagram, Facebook and YouTube, to create awareness and highlight the activities and achievements of the campaign.
As part of Special Campaign 6,
a
special one-day intensive drive was organised on 13th October 2026
, with a focus on accelerating the achievement of campaign targets through coordinated efforts across the Ministry and its Attached and Subordinate Offices. The activities undertaken included
tree plantation drives, intensive cleanliness campaigns and weeding out of old and redundant records
, along with other initiatives aimed at promoting environmental sustainability, improving workplace cleanliness and ensuring efficient records management. The drive witnessed enthusiastic participation across the Ministry and its organisations, contributing significantly to the achievement of the campaign's objectives.
The Ministry of Home Affairs reaffirmed its commitment to sustaining the momentum generated by Special Campaign 6, with continued emphasis on efficient service delivery, accountability, cleanliness and the promotion of a positive work culture. The active involvement of CAPFs and other affiliated organisations further strengthened the campaign and contributed significantly to its successful implementation.
Special Campaign 6 has not only contributed to cleaner and more organised workplaces but has also reinforced a culture of responsibility, transparency and efficiency across the Ministry and its field formations. The initiative reflects the Ministry's continued commitment to responsive governance, effective public service delivery and the institutionalisation of good administrative practices.

title: BRIC’s third Foundation Day celebrated at NII
subtitle:
India has potential to lead next biotechnology-driven industrial revolution, says Dr Jitendra Singh

Dr Jitendra Singh calls for stronger industry participation in India’s biotechnology ecosystem

BRIC’s integrated model is accelerating scientific collaboration while preserving institutional autonomy: Dr Jitendra Singh

BRIC and UK’s Centre for Process Innovation sign Letter of Intent to strengthen collaboration in biomanufacturing
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                10 NOV 2026 5:24PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Speaking today at the third Foundation Day of the Biotechnology Research and Innovation Council (BRIC), held at the BRIC–National Institute of Immunology (NII), Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology and Earth Sciences, and Minister of State in the Prime Minister’s Office, Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, the Department of Atomic Energy and the Department of Space, Dr Jitendra Singh said that India has potential next biotechnology-driven industrial revolution and called for deeper integration across scientific institutions and greater participation by industry in India’s biotechnology ecosystem.
Dr.Jitendra Singh said the Government had encouraged greater integration among science institutions to overcome silos and improve coordination. The Minister described BRIC as a “joint family” in which institutions pool resources while retaining their identities, independence and autonomy. The arrangement, he said, had reduced procedural delays associated with multiple directorates and approvals while creating opportunities for scientific collaboration. The Minister added that other departments and ministries had replicated the model.
Referring to the sector’s growth, Dr.Jitendra Singh said India’s bioeconomy had expanded from about USD 10 billion when the Government took office to more than USD 195 billion. He said the country’s biotechnology startup ecosystem had grown from around 50–60 startups to more than 11,000, with several showing global potential. The Minister also highlighted efforts to strengthen high-performance manufacturing through biomanufacturing hubs, biofoundries and AI-integrated biomanufacturing.
Dr.Jitendra Singh cited biofoundry hubs in Mohali, Hyderabad, Pune and Thiruvananthapuram, and said international partnerships, including the collaboration with the UK’s Centre for Process Innovation, would support further progress.
The Minister said the Genomics Centre of Excellence had attracted interest from medical institutions, including AIIMS. Dr. Singhsaid that genomics could support the shift towards precision medicine, with institutions beginning to adopt the approach and collaborate. Dr Singh also spoke about the i3C PhD programme, which enables scholars to immerse themselves in research, innovate and collaborate, including through placements in the health and agriculture sectors. He said nearly 200 students had benefited from the programme.
Dr. Singh said the Prime Minister’s Independence Day appeal to young people to explore new opportunities in biotechnology had generated enthusiasm across the sector. He also referred to outreach programmes for school students and the public, and recalled proposing a dedicated mentorship programme to encourage girls to pursue science.
Further, Dr.Jitendra Singh said the Government was opening more avenues for private-sector participation in science and research, drawing on experience from reforms in the nuclear sector. He referred to the Research, Development and Innovation Fund, the Anusandhan National Research Foundation and BIRAC as parts of the wider research and innovation landscape. He said India should be at the centre of the next industrial revolution, which he described as likely to be driven by biotechnology, artificial intelligence and genomics. Unlike earlier industrial revolutions that emerged elsewhere before India adopted their technologies, he said, the country’s biotechnology community had the opportunity to be at the forefront of the next one.
During the event, the Wellcome Trust announced a grant of up to ₹21.7 crore for a five-year immersion training programme for more than 250 iBRIC+ PhD scholars. A Letter of Intent was also signed between BRIC and the UK’s Centre for Process Innovation to strengthen India–UK collaboration in biomanufacturing and support the development of biofoundries.
Winners of the Festival of Sports were felicitated at the event. The iBRIC+ Spotlight Scientist of the Year–2026 awards were presented to Dr Sunil Laxman of BRIC-inStem, Dr Rashna Bhandari of BRIC-CDFD, and Prof.Bhabatosh Das, Professor at BRIC-THSTI
Dr Rajesh S. Gokhale, Secretary, Department of Biotechnology, and Director General, BRIC, emphasized that BRIC’s core vision is to move beyond isolated institutional excellence by unifying India’s 13 premier biotechnology institutions across 11 cities into a decentralised national network. Anchored in the pillars of people, culture, trust and resource allocation, and supported by a lean Secretariat and translational initiatives such as the i3C PhD curriculum and BRIC–BIRAC entrepreneurship programmes, the Council aims to connect laboratory innovation with market applications, advance sovereign technologies, strengthen food and health security, and establish India as a global biotechnology leader with lasting economic and societal impact
The event was also attended by Lt. Gen. (Retd.) Dr MadhuriKanitkar, Member, Prime Minister’s Science, Technology and Innovation Advisory Council (PM-STIAC), and former Vice-Chancellor of Maharashtra University of Health Sciences; Ms EktaVishnoi (IRS), Joint Secretary (Administration), Department of Biotechnology; and Dr Pushkar Sharma, Director, BRIC-NII.

title: Delhi's River Tourism Begins with the Launch of Yamuna Recreational Cruise Service
subtitle:

30-seater Electric Vessel launched along Sonia Vihar-Jagatpur stretch; initiative aims to boost Delhi's Sustainable Tourism

Yamuna’s Mythology and Heritage to Come Alive in Spectacular Light and Sound Show

Yamuna Cruise signals a new wave of river tourism in Delhi: Sarbananda Sonowal

Committed to develop Delhi's riverfront as an attractive public destination: Rekha Gupta
ministry: Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                10 NOV 2026 5:47PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Delhi took a significant step towards expanding its river-based tourism offerings with the inauguration of its first recreational Yamuna River Cruise service on the Yamuna by
Union Minister of Ports, Shipping and Waterways Sarbananda Sonowal
in presence of
Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta
at Sonia Vihar here today.
Developed along the Sonia Vihar-Jagatpur stretch, the initiative aims to unlock the tourism and recreational potential of the Yamuna while offering residents and visitors a new way to experience the national capital. The launch also marks another milestone in the Centre's efforts to develop India's rivers as vibrant avenues for tourism, passenger movement and economic activity.
The inauguration was attended by
Minister of State for Ports, Shipping and Waterways Shantanu Thakur; Minister of State for Road Transport and Highways Harsh Malhotra
;
Public Works Department and Irrigation and Flood Control Minister Parvesh Sahib Singh
;
Tourism Minister Kapil Mishra
;
Forest &
Environment
and Industries Minister Manjinder Singh Sirsa
and
MP Manoj Tiwari
, along with senior officials including Vijay Kumar, Secretary, Ministry of Ports, Shipping & Waterways; Rajeev Verma, Chief Secretary, Delhi Govt and Sushil Kumar Lohani, Chairman, Inland Waterways Authority of India (IWAI) among others from the Central and Delhi governments.
Speaking at the inauguration, Sarbananda Sonowal said the project reflected the government's commitment to harnessing India's vast inland waterways potential under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
“Under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, India's rivers and inland waterways are emerging as important drivers of economic growth, tourism and sustainable connectivity. The launch of Delhi's first recreational cruise service on the Yamuna is another step towards reconnecting people with our rivers and unlocking their immense potential. This launch signals a new wave of river tourism in the city. We are transforming waterways into avenues for tourism, trade and livelihoods while advancing our commitment to cleaner and more efficient mobility. This is an important part of our vision of building a Viksit Bharat,”
Sarbananda Sonowal
said.
The project features a 30-seater electric cruise vessel offering visitors a scenic experience along an approximately 6-kilometer round-trip stretch of the river. The use of electric-powered vessels highlights the potential of inland waterways for clean and sustainable mobility.
Chief Minister Rekha Gupta
said the initiative would add a new dimension to Delhi's tourism landscape and strengthen public engagement with the Yamuna.
“The Yamuna is an integral part of Delhi's history, culture and identity. This recreational cruise service will offer residents and visitors a new way to experience the river while creating fresh opportunities for tourism and local economic activity. Under the dynamic leadership of Prime Minister
Narendra Modi
,
we remain committed to develop Delhi's riverfront as an attractive public destination, with better amenities, sustainable infrastructure and experiences that celebrate the city's heritage,”
Rekha Gupta
said.
Envisioned as a wider eco-tourism destination, the Yamuna project includes a range of recreational attractions and visitor amenities. A key attraction is a musical fountain featuring a coordinated light and sound show depicting the history and spiritual significance of the Yamuna, including its association with Surya Dev, Yama and the divine leela of Shri Krishna, particularly the legendary Kaliya Daman.
The destination also includes a food court, shopping area, children's play zone and adventure sports facilities, including skating and rock climbing. Modern floating jetties, dedicated ticket counters and online booking facilities, restrooms, waiting areas and illuminated approach pathways have been incorporated to provide visitors with a convenient experience.
The Yamuna has been designated as National Waterway-110 under the National Waterways Act, 2016. The launch of the cruise service marks an important step towards developing the waterway for recreational navigation and river-based tourism in the national capital.
The initiative is part of a wider national transformation of India's inland waterways. Cargo movement on national waterways has increased from 18 million metric tonnes in 2013-14 to 218 million metric tonnes in 2025-26, reflecting the growing role of waterways in the country's logistics network. With freight movement costing an estimated ₹1.06 per tonne-kilometer on waterways, compared with ₹1.41 by rail and ₹2.28 by road, inland navigation offers a cost-effective alternative for transporting cargo.
River cruise tourism is another emerging dimension of this expansion. The number of river cruise vessels offering overnight journeys has increased from five in 2013-14 to 26 in 2025-26. The landmark journey of MV Ganga Vilas, recognised in the Limca Book of Records as the world's longest river cruise. Covering more than 3,200 kms across India and Bangladesh, the journey connected 50 tourist destinations, traversed two countries, five states and 27 river systems.
The Recreational Yamuna River Cruise Service has been developed by the Inland Waterways Authority of India under the
Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
in collaboration with the
Delhi Development Authority
,
Delhi Tourism and Transportation Development Corporation
,
Delhi Jal Board
and the
Irrigation and Flood Control Department
of the Delhi government.

content:
The Union Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, has invited citizens aged 18 years and above to register as volunteers under the
Vayo SAATHI
initiative, an important component of the recently launched ‘
Vayo Samman Rashtriya Abhiyan
’, a National Intergenerational Bonding Campaign under the
Atal Vayo Abhyuday Yojana
(AVYAY).
The initiative provides an opportunity for citizens, including students, young professionals and community volunteers, to contribute towards the welfare, dignity and social inclusion of senior citizens.
The Vayo SAATHI initiative stands for
Support, Awareness, Assistance, Training, Health and Inclusion
. Under this initiative, registered volunteers will act as friends, facilitators and connectors for senior citizens, supporting their social inclusion and overall well-being. Volunteers will also receive a
Vayo SAATHI
Certificate in recognition of their participation.
The Ministry encourages all eligible citizens to register as
Vayo SAATHI Volunteers
and contribute their time, skills and efforts towards building an inclusive society where every senior citizen is valued, respected and supported.
A Senior Official in the Ministry informed that the citizens interested in joining the initiative can register through
Senior Citizens Welfare (SCW) Single Access Mechanism For All Verticals of Empowerment And Social Harmony (SAMAVESH)
Portal on
https://seniorcitizen.dosje.gov.in/vayo-sathi
and become part of a nationwide effort to strengthen intergenerational relationships and promote active participation of senior citizens in society.
He said the interested citizens can also access the Vayo SAATHI volunteer registration facility, Or JEEVAN (Joint Elderly Empowerment & Virtual Assistance Network) mobile application to register and participate in the initiative.
The Official said the initiative encourages volunteers to assist senior citizens in accessing digital services, welfare-related information and community support. It also seeks to promote digital literacy, awareness about cyber fraud, health and wellness, and greater social participation among older persons.
The Official said Dr. Virendra Kumar, Union Minister for Social Justice and Empowerment recently launched the national level
Vayo Samman Rashtriya Abhiyan
in the National Capital. He said the Campaign aims to strengthen intergenerational solidarity by bringing together the experience, wisdom and knowledge of senior citizens with the energy and capabilities of younger generations.
The Abhiyan is based on the ‘5C’ model – Connect, Converse, Co-create, Contribute and Continue – which seeks to establish sustained engagement between generations, he said.
It encourages younger and older generations to connect through community platforms and educational institutions, share experiences and stories, undertake joint activities, exchange knowledge and skills, and continue such engagement as a regular community-led practice, the Official added.
He further said the Campaign encompasses twelve thematic areas, including ‘30 Minutes Together’, ‘Teach Me – I'll Teach You’, ‘My Story, My India’, ‘Digital Dada-Dadi / Digital Saathi’, ‘Generation Health & Wellness’ and ‘Silver Skills – Seniors as Mentors’.
These themes aim to promote companionship, preserve oral histories, enhance digital literacy, create awareness about cyber fraud, encourage health and wellness, and recognise senior citizens as mentors and valuable contributors to society, he said.
The official said that the Vayo SAATHI initiative provides a meaningful platform for citizens to contribute towards the well-being of senior citizens through simple but impactful activities, such as spending time with them, helping them access digital services, sharing knowledge and skills, and facilitating their participation in community activities.
The campaign seeks to reach every village and neighbourhood through Panchayats, local bodies, educational institutions and community institutions. It encourages families, youth organisations, universities, Non-Governmental Organisations (NGOs), Resident Welfare Associations (RWAs) and Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) partners to actively participate in the initiative and mobilise volunteers.
The Ministry has also released a Handbook on
Vayo Samman Rashtriya Abhiyan
, providing a comprehensive guiding framework covering the objectives, implementation strategy, thematic activities and roles of States, Districts and community institutions in carrying forward the campaign.
Through the Vayo Samman Rashtriya Abhiyan, the Ministry seeks to foster a stronger culture of respect, care, companionship and solidarity across generations. The initiative recognises senior citizens not merely as beneficiaries of welfare programmes but as active contributors, mentors and valuable repositories of knowledge, culture and social experience.

The Ministry has been organising Shilp Samagam Melas since 2022. Through these fairs, more than 1,000 artisans from Scheduled Castes, Other Backward Classes and Safai Karamchari communities have benefited from opportunities to exhibit and market their products.

ज्योति

The Mela showcases a diverse range of handicrafts, handloom products, traditional textiles, festive decorations, lamps, home décor items and other indigenous products through more than 130 stalls.
The exhibition provides an accessible marketing platform for artisans and beneficiaries to connect directly with consumers, expand their market reach and strengthen their entrepreneurial capabilities.
The Mela also provides opportunities for artisans to expand their market reach through initiatives such as Bharat TULIP, which connects artisans with e-commerce platforms, and Purple Fest, which celebrates the creativity and capabilities of persons with disabilities while promoting inclusion and equal opportunities.
The Mela has witnessed visits by Hon'ble Union Minister for Social Justice and Empowerment, Dr. Virendra Kumar; Union Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment, Shri Ramdas Athawale; Union Minister of State for Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution, Smt. A major attraction of the Mela is the series of cultural activities and programmes hosted every evening at the Manch. Citizens, families and young visitors are enthusiastically visiting the Mela to explore the diverse range of traditional products, appreciate the craftsmanship of participating artisans and support their efforts towards entrepreneurship, economic empowerment and self-reliance.

content:
The journey of 60 year Mr Subramanian
(name changed),
reflects the importance of ensuring occupational safety, health protection and livelihood security for sanitation workers.
Through the NAMASTE Scheme, access to protective equipment and awareness training has helped him continue his profession with greater confidence, improved well-being and dignity. His experience highlights how targeted interventions under the NAMASTE Scheme are contributing towards safer working conditions, better livelihood opportunities and a more dignified future for sanitation workers.
Mr Subramanian, a sanitation worker from Pondicherry Municipality, belonging to the Scheduled Caste community, had spent over 15 years undertaking the demanding work of sewer and septic tank cleaning. Throughout his working life, he was frequently exposed to hazardous conditions, often without adequate protective equipment or occupational safety measures. Prolonged exposure to hazardous waste resulted in recurring skin infections and respiratory discomfort, affecting his ability to work regularly and maintain his health.
As the sole earning member of a family of four, his health-related challenges placed considerable financial pressure on the household. Frequent medical expenses further strained the family's limited resources, while his modest monthly income of approximately Rs. 12,000 made it difficult to manage household requirements. Despite these hardships, he remained committed to his profession and aspired to continue earning a livelihood with dignity while ensuring his safety and well-being.
A significant change came in 2025 through the National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem (NAMASTE) Scheme, implemented by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. Under the scheme, he received a comprehensive Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) kit comprising protective overalls, heavy-duty gloves, gumboots, a face mask and a safety helmet. He also underwent awareness training on safe sanitation practices and the prevention of occupational health risks.
The provision of protective equipment and safety awareness brought a meaningful improvement to his working conditions. With better protection against occupational hazards, his health improved considerably, work-related absences reduced and medical expenses declined. Improved health and greater consistency at work also contributed to an increase in his monthly income from approximately Rs. 12,000 to Rs. 16,000–18,000, strengthening his financial stability.

title: Press Note on Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) Quarterly Bulletin July-September 2026
subtitle:
LFPR and WPR improved in both rural and urban areas

Rural UR declined

Gain in employment in agriculture sector in rural areas
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                10 NOV 2026 4:00PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Snapshots:
The overall LFPR for persons (15+ years) reported an increase to 55.5% in July-September, 2026
compared to 54.6% in the previous quarter.
Rural LFPR (15+ years) recorded at 58.1%, an increase of 0.9 percentage points compared with same period of last year.
Overall WPR (15+ years) stood at 52.7% during July-September, 2026, registering an increase of 1.0 percentage point over the previous quarter.
Rural WPR increased by 1.4 percentage points quarter-on-quarter to 55.6% during July-September, 2026.
The share of regular wage/ salaried employment in urban areas reported an increase of 0.3 percentage points to 49.6% compared to the previous quarter.
During July-September, 2026 the share of self-employed in rural areas increased by 1.3 percentage points to 62.7% compared with last quarter.
Rural agricultural employment increased by 3.8 percentage points over the quarter to 56.7% during July-September, 2026
.
Rural UR declined to 4.3% during July-September, 2026 from 4.8% in the previous quarter.
Introduction
The Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) conducted by NSO, MoSPI, is the primary source of data on activity participation and employment-unemployment conditions of the population. The PLFS survey methodology has been modified from January, 2025 to provide monthly and quarterly estimates of labour force indicators for both rural and urban India under the CWS framework.
Considering the need to generate high-frequency labour force indicators with wider coverage, the sampling methodology of the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) was revamped from January, 2025. The redesigned PLFS aims to achieve the following objectives:
To generate key employment and unemployment indicators – namely Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR), Worker Population Ratio (WPR) and Unemployment Rate (UR) – every month for both rural and urban areas at the all-India level under the Current Weekly Status (CWS).
To extend the Quarterly PLFS results to rural areas, thereby producing quarterly estimates of labour market indicators for both rural and urban India under the CWS framework.
To provide annual estimates of key employment and unemployment indicators in both Usual Status (ps+ss) and Current Weekly Status (CWS) for rural as well as urban areas.
Earlier PLFS Quarterly Bulletins released up to December, 2024, presented labour market indicators only for urban areas. The Bulletin for April – June, 2025 marked the first in the series to provide estimates for both rural and urban areas and the current Bulletin for July – September, 2026 is the sixth in the series. In this Quarterly Bulletin
, efforts have also been made to provide estimates of the number of workers in absolute terms
.
This Quarterly Bulletin presents estimates of key labour force indicators —
Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR), Worker Population Ratio (WPR), Unemployment Rate (UR), and
the distribution of workers by broad employment status and industry of work —
in the Current Weekly Status (CWS), separately for rural and urban areas at the all-India level. In addition, state-level estimates of LFPR, WPR, and UR in CWS are also provided for selected States.
Key findings for persons of age 15 years and above following CWS:
Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR) improved in both rural and urban sectors:
Overall LFPR for persons of age 15 years and above increased to 55.5% during July-September, 2026 from 54.6% in the previous quarter. The improvement was driven by an increase in LFPR for both the rural and urban areas. In rural areas, LFPR for persons of age 15 years and above rose to 58.1% in the current quarter from 56.9% in the previous quarter. Similarly, urban LFPR increased marginally to 50.4% from 50.2% during the same period.
The overall female LFPR increased to 34.7% during the current quarter from 33.2% in the previous quarter. Among male, the urban LFPR registered a marginal increase, reaching 77.3% during the quarter from 77.0% in the quarter April-June, 2026.
On a year-on-year basis, the overall LFPR recorded an increase of 0.4 percentage points, rising from 55.1% in July-September, 2025 to 55.5% in July-September, 2026. Rural LFPR also improved by 0.9 percentage points, increasing from 57.2% to 58.1% during the same period, while the urban LFPR declined marginally by 0.3 percentage points.
Overall LFPR for persons aged 15 years and above stood at 55.5% during July-September 2026, registering an increase over both the previous quarter and the corresponding quarter of 2025
Workforce participation increased:
Overall Worker Population Ratio (WPR) for persons of age 15 years and above increased to
52.7% during the quarter July-September, 2026, from 51.7% in the previous quarter. WPR in rural areas increased to 55.6% from 54.2% in the last quarter. In urban areas, WPR remained largely stable at 46.9% during July-September, 2026, compared with 46.8% in April-June, 2026. Among male, WPR increased to 73.4% in the current quarter from 73.0% in the previous quarter, while the female WPR rose notably to 32.8% from 31.3% over the same period.
In comparison with the corresponding quarter of the previous year, the overall WPR increased by 0.5 percentage points during July-September, 2026. Rural WPR also recorded an increase of 0.9 percentage points over the same period. Urban WPR maintained stability in the current quarter compared with the previous year.
Compared with the previous quarter, WPR improved for both male and female aged 15 years and above, reaching 73.4% and 32.8%, respectively, in July-September 2026.
Overall and rural Unemployment Rate (UR) declined:
Overall UR for persons of age 15 years and above improved to 5.1% during the current quarter, compared with 5.4% in the previous quarter. During the same period, the rural UR fell to 4.3% from 4.8%, while urban UR remained broadly stable at 6.8 % against 6.7% in the previous quarter.
Compared with the corresponding quarter of 2025, the rural UR remained largely unchanged at 4.3% during July-September, 2026 compared with 4.4% during July-September, 2025. Rural male UR declined by 0.3 percentage points to 4.4% during July-September, 2026 from 4.7% during July-September, 20265. Urban UR registered marginal improvements for both male (6.2% to 6.1%) and female (9.0% to 8.8%) over the same period.
Overall UR for persons of age 15 years and above improved to 5.1% in July-September, 2026 compared to 5.4% in previous quarter.
Rural self-employment and urban regular wage/ salaried employment increased:
The
share of workers in rural areas engaged in self-employment increased to 62.7% in the current quarter from 61.4% in previous quarter. In urban areas, share of regular wage/ salaried workers increased to 49.6% from 49.3% in the previous quarter. In both rural and urban areas, the share of workers engaged in casual labour declined during July–September, 2026 compared with the previous quarter. In rural areas, it decreased from 22.5% to 21.7%, while in urban areas, it declined from 11.1% to 10.7%.
A year-on-year comparison indicates a reduction in the proportion of workers engaged in casual labour employment. In rural areas, the share declined by 0.5 percentage points from 22.2% in July-September, 2025 to 21.7% in July-September 2026. Similarly, in urban areas, it decreased marginally by 0.2 percentage points from 10.9% to 10.7% during the same period. In rural areas, share of workers in self-employment remained stable while regular wage/ salaried employment increased by 0.6 percentage points over the year. In urban areas, self-employment increased by 0.4 percentage point, while for regular wage/ salaried employment declined marginally in comparison with the same quarter of last year.
The share of workers engaged in casual labour employment declined during July-September, 2026, both quarter-on-quarter and year-on-year
Share of agriculture sector increased in rural areas, tertiary sector remained stable in urban areas:
The sectoral distribution of employment continued to reflect the distinct rural–urban employment patterns, with the rural workforce predominantly engaged in agriculture and the urban workforce concentrated in the tertiary sector. In rural areas, the share of workers engaged in agriculture increased from 52.9% in April–June, 2026 to 56.7% in July–September, 2026. The share of workers engaged in the secondary sector, including mining and quarrying, stood at 21.9% against 24.4% in the previous quarter. In the tertiary sector, it is estimated at 21.4% in the current quarter against 22.7% in the last quarter.
Compared with July–September, 2025, the share of rural workers engaged in the secondary sector, including mining and quarrying, increased from 21.0% to 21.9%, while the share in the tertiary sector remained broadly stable, increasing marginally from 21.3% to 21.4% in July–September, 2026. In urban areas, the share of workers engaged in secondary and tertiary sectors remained broadly stable.
Over the year, rural employment shares in the secondary sector rose from 21.0% to 21.9%, while the tertiary sector remained stable at around 21.4%
Using the projected population figures of the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MoHFW), the absolute number of workers aged 15 years and above has been estimated. On average, 57.9 crore persons aged 15 years and above were employed in the country during the quarter July-September, 2026, of which 40.5 crore were male and 17.4 crore were female.

https://www.mospi.gov.in
).

through Neighbourhood Youth Parliaments during Week 8 of the
‘Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat’
100-Week Sankalp Abhiyan on November 6 and 7, 2026. The two initiatives combined Diwali celebrations with grassroots discussions on substance abuse, mobilising over 1.19 lakh youth and citizens across 30 States/UTs with participants taking pledges towards a Nasha Mukt Bharat.
Under the
‘Nasha Mukt Yuva Deepotsav – Ek Diya Sankalp Ka’
initiative, 435 programmes and 568 activities were organised, drawing participation from 1,10,101 people. Activities included rangoli formations, diya lighting, sweets distribution, awareness programmes and felicitation of MY Bharat volunteers. Partner organisations, including Brahma Kumaris, EPSI and Heartfulness, also participated.
In Uttar Pradesh, MY Bharat organised celebrations with volunteers in Lucknow, distributed sweets and fruits at an old-age home in Banda, and conducted awareness activities in Rampur. In Chhattisgarh, Deepotsav and rangoli activities were organised in Mungeli and Dhamtari. In Himachal Pradesh, celebrations and sweets distribution were organised at an old-age home in Kangra. Similar activities were held in Yavatmal, Maharashtra; Yanam, Puducherry; and Jammu and Kashmir.
The
‘Nasha Mukt Yuva Par Paricharcha’
initiative, organised through Neighbourhood Youth Parliaments (NYPs) at the block level, recorded 85 programmes and 298 activities, with participation from 9,526 individuals. The discussions focused on substance abuse, its challenges and the role of young people in building a drug-free society.
Each NYP was designed to engage at least 80 young people per block through four structured sessions. These covered a briefing on the MY Bharat portal; ‘Understanding Substance Abuse: Challenges before India’s Youth’; ‘From Awareness to Action: Tools for a Nasha Mukt Yuva’; and an audio-visual presentation titled ‘Stories of Change: The Journey Towards a Nasha Mukt Bharat’.
The discussions also included slogan writing, rangoli formations, street plays, interactive sessions and pledge-taking. Such activities were organised in Bhuna in Fatehabad, Haryana; Latur in Maharashtra; East Delhi; and Dongargarh Block in Chhattisgarh. The ‘Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat’ 100-Week Sankalp Abhiyan continues to provide a nationwide platform for sustained youth engagement and community-led action towards a drug-free India.
